source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Allen, Texas campus publishes 77 MW of IT capacity, 16 percent of all published data center power in Texas, where only 19 of 133 mapped facilities publish any figure.

The capacity sits in one operator across three contiguous facility codes, DFW3 through DFW5, with 976,000 square feet of technical space. That concentration is real, but the share is measured against a partial denominator. Most of the state's mapped data centers publish no power number at all, so the Texas market is substantially unmeasured and the 16 percent describes the visible portion rather than the whole.

IT capacity is the figure that bounds how many accelerators a building can hold. At 40 kW per rack, 77 MW works out to roughly 1,925 racks, which is an assumption about density and utilization rather than a claim by the operator. The campus also carries certifications for payment card, healthcare, information security, federal systems, audit reporting, and environmental design, which qualifies it for regulated workloads that many sites cannot serve.

What the data does not include is total power consumption, PUE, grid interconnection capacity, water usage, or power source composition. Without those, 77 MW of IT load cannot be converted into a statement about whether grid supply or cooling limits the site, and the campus cannot be read as either an enabler or a constraint on regional GPU deployment. The suitability score of 76 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion listed as missing, so it describes what exists rather than what is planned.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
